conventions.f16: little-endian uint16 bit pattern per value
conventions.window_index: window (i, j) of 51.6 has index w = j*nwx + i; window token t = 8*ly + lx; nwx = ceil((Nx + sx)/8), nwy = ceil((Ny + sy)/8) with the effective shift
conventions.shift: shift_row = the stage's SH row; recurrent halves use ((s + 4) mod 8) (effective_shift)
conventions.Tb: Tb[h][k] is the stored 16 x 16 block of pair k in the order of 51.3 step 2: (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1),(0,2),(1,2),(0,3),(1,3),(2,2),(3,2),(2,3),(3,3) (PROVISIONAL, QUESTIONS-51.md Q1)
conventions.E1_input: E1 'in' is the level-1 tensor with 128 channels as stored by IN0 (page 52); the reference does not interpret the channel order (QUESTIONS-51.md Q2)
conventions.synthetic: all weights and constants are synthetic test inputs (page 57 not available); ranges in QUESTIONS-51.md Q3

e4m3_network.row_sum: 51.3 step 4 / 51.8 item 1: bit-exact when the row sums Z of intermediates/Z are supplied. With an implementation's own Z (f32 accumulation, any order) Z differs by one f16 step in about 22 % of the rows and P codes then differ by at most one code step in those rows; spec 51 states no bound for the downstream outputs in that case
e4m3_network.matrix_step: 51.1: the required matrix step rounds once to f16 per 32-input step; an implementation that accumulates longer chains in higher precision may differ by an occasional one-step difference in a quantised intermediate (not bit-exact then)

f16_hidden.row_sum: 51.3 step 4 / 51.8 item 1: bit-exact when the row sums Z of intermediates/Z are supplied. With an implementation's own Z (f32 accumulation, any order) Z differs by one f16 step in about 22 % of the rows and P codes then differ by at most one code step in those rows; spec 51 states no bound for the downstream outputs in that case
f16_hidden.matrix_step: 51.1: the required matrix step rounds once to f16 per 32-input step; an implementation that accumulates longer chains in higher precision may differ by an occasional one-step difference in a quantised intermediate (not bit-exact then)
f16_hidden.sigmoid: 51.4: a conforming sig may give the reference or one of its two f16 neighbours where the reference f32 value lies within about 2^-21 of an f16 midpoint; tokens whose hidden update used such a sigmoid input are flagged in the 'sig_near_mask' file (1 = may differ)

f16_rowsum.note: reference Z = exact sum of the 64 weights rounded once (WrongGPU's choice); an f32 accumulation in any order may differ by one f16 step (51.3 step 4)

files: binary files are not committed (clean-repo content gate): regenerate them with the generator; SHA256SUMS lists every file, check_vectors verifies it

d8.rule: 51.1 d8 of all 256 codes (NaN for 0x7F/0xFF, -0 for 0x80)

q8_of_f16.rule: 51.1 Q8 of every f16 pattern (51.8 item 3)

tolerance.allowed: reference or one of its two f16 neighbours where sig_near = 1 (51.4, 51.8 item 4)

sig_near.rule: 1 where the reference f32 s lies within 4 f32 ulps (about 2^-21 relative) of an f16 rounding midpoint

recip.rule: 51.3 step 4 r = R(1/Z) of every f16 pattern

attn_w_A.rule: 51.3 step 3 w(s) for every f16 score (51.8 item 2)

act_A.rule: 51.3 step 8 act(x) for every f16 x (51.8 item 2)

attn_w_B.rule: 51.3 step 3 w(s) for every f16 score (51.8 item 2)

act_B.rule: 51.3 step 8 act(x) for every f16 x (51.8 item 2)

attn_w_zovf.rule: 51.3 step 3 w(s) for every f16 score (51.8 item 2)

act_zovf.rule: 51.3 step 8 act(x) for every f16 x (51.8 item 2)

zovf.note: 64 * w_max reaches the f16 overflow threshold: rows with Z = +inf occur

Z.use: supply to the implementation for the bit-exact comparison (51.8 item 1)
